Subcutaneous injection - not affected by food

summary: Nadroparin calcium is a low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) anticoagulant used to prevent and treat venous thromboembolism, in acute coronary syndromes, and to prevent clotting in the extracorporeal circuit during haemodialysis. It acts mainly by potentiating antithrombin-mediated inhibition of factor Xa. Given subcutaneously (once or twice daily) with predictable response, it usually does not require routine monitoring, but platelet counts (for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia) and dose adjustment in renal impairment are important. It is not FDA-approved but is widely used under EMA/SmPC and BNF labeling.
indications: Prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism (e.g., surgical and high-risk medical patients)
Treatment of established deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
Treatment of unstable angina / non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (acute coronary syndrome)
Prevention of clotting in the extracorporeal circuit during haemodialysis

dosage.d: 2850 anti-Xa IU (0.3 mL) SC once daily
dosage.n: Start ~2 h before surgery; continue ~7-10 days

dosage.d: Weight-adjusted (e.g., 38 anti-Xa IU/kg) SC once daily
dosage.n: Increase after surgery per protocol; weight-based

dosage.d: 85-86 anti-Xa IU/kg SC every 12 hours (or 171 IU/kg once daily)
dosage.n: Overlap with oral anticoagulant until therapeutic

dosage.d: 86 anti-Xa IU/kg SC every 12 hours with aspirin
Single dose into arterial line at session start, weight-based
dosage.n: Adjust for session length and bleeding risk

admin: Administer by deep subcutaneous injection, usually into the anterolateral or posterolateral abdominal wall, alternating sides
Do not expel the air bubble from prefilled syringes; insert the full needle into a skin fold and hold the fold during injection
Do not give by intramuscular injection
For haemodialysis, inject into the arterial line of the circuit
Avoid rubbing the injection site to reduce bruising
moa: Nadroparin is a low molecular weight heparin that binds to antithrombin III, markedly accelerating the inhibition of activated factor X (factor Xa) and, to a lesser degree, thrombin (factor IIa). Compared with unfractionated heparin it has a higher anti-Xa to anti-IIa activity ratio, giving a more predictable anticoagulant response, better subcutaneous bioavailability, and a longer half-life.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to nadroparin or heparins
History of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) with nadroparin or other heparins
Recent CNS, eye, or ear surgery / haemorrhagic stroke
relative: Severe renal impairment (avoid therapeutic doses; reduce prophylactic)
Peptic ulcer or other bleeding-prone lesions

preg: LMWHs do not cross the placenta and are the anticoagulants of choice when anticoagulation is required in pregnancy. Use under specialist guidance with appropriate dose adjustment; avoid multidose vials containing benzyl alcohol.
lact: Excretion into breast milk is minimal and oral absorption by the infant is negligible. Nadroparin is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: Renally eliminated, so it accumulates in renal impairment. Reduce the dose in moderate impairment and avoid therapeutic dosing in severe impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min); consider unfractionated heparin or anti-Xa monitoring instead.
hepatic: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment because of increased bleeding risk from impaired clotting factor synthesis.

major: Other anticoagulants (vitamin K antagonists, DOACs, unfractionated heparin) - additive bleeding risk; avoid overlap except as planned bridging
Systemic salicylates/NSAIDs at anti-inflammatory doses - increased bleeding risk
moderate: Antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel, ticagrelor) - additive bleeding risk; use only when indicated
Drugs causing hyperkalaemia (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, potassium-sparing diuretics) - additive risk with heparin-induced aldosterone suppression
minor: Glyceryl trinitrate infusion (may reduce heparin effect - relevant mainly to UFH)
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; excessive intake may add to bleeding/fall risk
interactions.diagnostics: Monitored by anti-Xa activity (not aPTT) when indicated; may cause raised transaminases and hyperkalaemia

emergency: Spinal/epidural haematoma (back pain, leg weakness, bladder/bowel dysfunction)

monitoring: Platelet count at baseline and periodically (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia)
Renal function, especially in the elderly and at-risk patients
Anti-Xa activity in selected patients (renal impairment, extremes of weight, pregnancy)
counsel: This medicine is injected under the skin, usually in the abdomen - alternate sites and do not rub afterwards
Bruising at the injection site is common and not usually serious
Report unusual or prolonged bleeding, black stools, blood in urine, or a severe headache
Seek urgent help for back pain, leg weakness, or loss of bladder/bowel control after spinal anaesthesia
Tell all healthcare providers you are on a blood thinner before any procedure
Avoid additional pain relievers like aspirin/ibuprofen unless approved by your doctor
pk: Anti-Xa activity detectable soon after subcutaneous injection
Peak anti-Xa activity at approximately 3-5 hours after SC dosing
Anti-Xa half-life approximately 3.5 hours (longer in renal impairment)
Anticoagulant effect supports once- or twice-daily dosing
Store below 25-30 C; do not freeze; keep prefilled syringes in the original packaging
pearls: NOTE: Nadroparin is NOT FDA-approved; this record follows EMA/SmPC and BNF labeling rather than US prescribing information
Monitored by anti-Xa activity, not aPTT, when laboratory monitoring is needed
Renally cleared - reduce dose or avoid therapeutic use in severe renal impairment
Check platelets to detect heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
Protamine only partially reverses LMWH anti-Xa activity
Observe neuraxial-anaesthesia timing rules to avoid spinal haematoma
missed: Inject the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule - do not inject a double dose. For weight-based treatment regimens follow your clinician's specific advice.
overdose: Overdose can cause haemorrhagic complications. Minor bleeding rarely needs specific treatment. For significant bleeding, protamine sulphate partially neutralises the anti-Xa effect (it does not fully reverse LMWH); give supportive care, transfusion as needed, and stop the drug. Anti-Xa monitoring can guide management.
